sentences.text: 2. Let necessary insertion in the cause title of the present writ petition be made by learned counsel for the petitioner in course of the day.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that two copies of the writ petition have already been served to Ms. Sweety Topno, learned counsel for the respondent No.6.
4.

The present writ petition has been filed for issuance of direction upon the concerned respondents to pay the balance amount of compensation to the petitioner for acquisition of his land appertaining to Jamabandi No. 25, Survey Plot No. 199, Village-Fatehpur, Thana No. 30, measuring an area of 0.2518 Acre for widening and realignment of NH-80.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the aforesaid land is recorded in the name of Bhawra Dhanged.
The petitioner is the son of Prabhu Dhanged @ Prabhu Muryari and the great grandson of the recorded tenant, namely, Bhawra Dhanged (since deceased).

In the process of acquisition of the said land, Land Acquisition Case No. 50/2016-17 was initiated and notice under Section 3H of the National Highways Act, 1956 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act, 1956') [wrongly mentioned as Section 37(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 in the said notice-Annexure-1 to the writ petition

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: ] was issued in the name of the petitioner's great grandfather by the District Land Acquisition Officer, Sahebganj-cum-Competent Authority under the Act, 1956 fixing compensation of Rs.8,07,549.04/-.

The grievance of the petitioner is that out of the said compensation amount,
only Rs.5,00,596/- has been paid to him, however, the balance amount of Rs.3,06,953.04 has not been paid despite several representations made to the authorities in this regard.
Under the said compelling circumstance, the petitioner has preferred the present writ petition.

6. Mr. Krishna Kr. Bhatt, learned A.C to S.C-I appearing on behalf of the State-respondents as well as Ms. Sweety Topno, learned counsel for the respondent-NHAI, jointly submit that the aforesaid contention of the petitioner is required to be factually examined by the respondent No.4 and hence if he prefers a fresh application before the said respondent in this regard, an appropriate decision will be taken within a time frame.
7. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and keeping in view the nature of the prayer made in the present writ petition, without entering into the merit of the petitioner's aforesaid contention, he is given liberty to prefer a fresh application before the respondent No.4 in this regard.

On receipt of the said application, the respondent No.4, after verifying the relevant records and on providing an opportunity of hearing to the petitioner/his representative, shall take an appropriate informed decision within one month from the date of filing of the said application.
8. The present writ petition is accordingly disposed of with the aforesaid liberty and direction.

Satish/- (RAJESH SHANKAR, J)
